Hoje olho para trás e agradeço ao João por ter insistido para eu jogar. O que começou com muita raiva e várias mortes acabou se tornando uma das minhas experiências favoritas nos videogames. ⚔️🔥🎮

通关这款ARPG界原审，我给出如下评价：
不明觉厉的地图设计，莫名其妙的碎片剧情，狗屎一坨的数值，还有乱七八糟的人/怪成长曲线，构成了这么一个所谓的经典魂游，不出圈是应该的，作为一款以动作交互为卖点之一的游戏却没有一项动作有关的优点：人物翻滚闪避屎一样的粘滞感，单一的动作系统，没有一招一式，只有像区一样的偷刀翻滚无限循环。所谓的交互设计仿佛江郎才尽，只能靠硬上敌怪机制和数值的同时对玩家进行动作限制才能让玩家进行所谓的交互。游戏本身有着不错的美术设计和具有独创性的机制，但缺点又严重的盖过了这些部分，喜欢的玩家更多的是处于潜意识对当时受难的自己的怜悯，所以要在通关后告诉自己：“这是一部好游戏，我受到的苦难是为了通关后的苦尽甘来，我尝到了这份游戏的优秀，我喜欢这个游戏”。来催眠自己，另一部分是游戏仿佛曲高和寡的设计吸引那部分仿佛自己是宫崎英高的伯乐的一群人，实际上是对这一坨要剧情没剧情，要动作没动作，只剩下为难而难的答辩设计的自嗨，当特立独行成为习惯，你竭尽全力找到的所谓“高山流水”成了你拼死都要守护的白月光.
庆幸此游不会成为大众习惯上的行业标杆，否则游戏圈终无创新可言。

This is one of those games that makes you suffer a little, then makes you thank it for the experience. The combat feels sharp, heavy, and fair in that painful Dark Souls way. When you die, most of the time you know exactly what you did wrong, and when you finally beat a boss that was destroying you for an hour, it feels amazing.

The atmosphere is a huge part of why it works. Everything feels dark, tired, beautiful, and dangerous, like the whole world is already falling apart and you’re just walking through the last pieces of it. The areas, enemies, music, armor, weapons, and boss designs all have that strong FromSoftware style where you don’t always understand everything, but you still feel the weight of it.

I also love how much personality there is in different builds and weapons. You can play careful, aggressive, heavy, fast, weird, stupid — and somehow the game lets you make it work if you learn what you’re doing.

It’s hard, yes, but not in an empty way. It gives you frustration, then skill, then confidence, then one of the best feelings you can get from a game. Easy recommendation if you like dark fantasy, tough bosses, and earning every win.

My Dark Souls III Review.

SCORE SUMMARY:
• Story: 8.5/10
• Gameplay: 9/10
• Atmosphere: 8.5/10
• Soundtrack: 10/10
OVERALL SCORE: 8.5/10

DETAILED COMMENTS:
• Story
 The game brings the trilogy to a close by showing the kingdom of Lothric on the brink of its end, with the First Flame fading away. Due to the lack of a hero, a bell resurrects the ancient Lords of Cinder (Aldrich, the Abyss Watchers, and Yhorm the Giant) to serve as fuel once again, but they refuse their purpose. In the face of this desertion, we are reborn as the Ashen One and set out on a hunt for the Lords with the support of the Firekeeper and Ludleth, the only Lord who remained faithful.
Our journey begins with the Abyss Watchers, a legion inspired by Artorias that ended up corrupted by the very Abyss they swore to fight. Next, we face Aldrich, an ancient cannibalistic monk transformed into a creature of mud who, manipulated by the tyrant Pontiff Sulyvahn, heads to Anor Londo to devour the ancient gods, such as Gwyndolin. The third Lord is Yhorm, a kind giant who sacrificed himself for a people who hated him; devastated upon seeing his capital destroyed after his return, he lost his will to live and is defeated by us with the help of his great friend Siegward of Catarina, who fulfills an old promise to give him a dignified rest.
The last Lord is Prince Lothric who, born weak and sharing his soul with his older brother Lorian, was influenced by a mentor to question the cycle and reject his sacrifice, isolating himself at the top of the castle. Before confronting him, the game presents secrets such as the driven-mad King Oceiros and his invisible son Ocelotte, as well as the Nameless King, Gwyn's firstborn son who was erased from history for allying with the dragons.
The DLCs expand this search for a new beginning. In the Painted World of Ariandel, we defeat Sister Friede to allow the rotting world to burn and be reborn. In the Ringed City, we face the knight Gael, corrupted after devouring the Pygmies to obtain the pigment of the Dark Soul. Upon delivering this blood to the young painter, she creates a new cold, dark, and gentle world, free from previous cycles. Finally, gathering the power of the Lords at the Furnace of the First Flame, we defeat the Soul of Cinder and face three choices: prolong the cycle, usurp the flame as the Lord of Hollows, or let the fire die out, with the Firekeeper nurturing the hope that new sparks will be reborn in the future.
• Gameplay
 Now we see the true pinnacle of the trilogy's gameplay; compared to the previous games, you'll notice a huge leap forward, making it much faster and more fluid. I confess I missed the lifegems and the bonfire ascetics of the last game.
 The boss fights are the best in the trilogy; the bosses in this new game are much more aggressive, with various combos that can eradicate you with extreme ease. You are forced to keep up with the fast pace that the game offers, but it also rewards you for it, for example with critical attacks.
 About the bossfights, ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥! They are incredible, most of the bosses make you feel like you're in a restless dance, the fight choreography is perfect. The best game for me is against Sister Friede, what a perfect fight! The amount of time I spent dying and getting mad against her is nothing compared to how sensational this fight is, she punishes you severely if you get distracted for even a second. I was so happy when I killed her in the second phase... But when I saw that another health bar had gone up, I was simply in disbelief and cursed a lot, when you learn to fight with her in the three phases the bossfight becomes a deadly and frenetic dance to the point of leaving you breathless, and I dare say it's one of the top 3 best bossfights in Dark Souls.
• Atmosphere
The setting of this game is very good, however, when compared to the previous games, I found it the weakest of the three, since this one is quite linear instead of giving us the freedom to forge our own path.
We start separated by a cemetery until we find our main lobby: Firelink Shrine, our safe haven with the thrones, a floor covered in ashes, and beloved NPCs like the Firekeeper and blacksmith Andre, alongside cool references like the giant tree and the crows' nest. From there we go to Lothric, catching a glimpse of a once-great kingdom filled with rubble and corpses, before heading to the Undead Settlement with its makeshift wooden huts and hunting evangelists, and Farron Keep, a poisonous swamp filled with crucified bodies. We then proceed through the dark catacombs to Smouldering Lake and the ruins of Izalith, filled with demon bodies.
After leaving the catacombs, we arrive at the most beautiful view in the game (competing with Majula): Irithyll of the Boreal Valley. A gigantic city bathed in snow under a breathtaking aurora borealis. While exploring, we reach Anor Londo which, unlike the first game, is now covered in snow and bathed in moonlight, featuring our dead giant blacksmith friend and the cathedral abandoned and bathed in the putrid mud of Aldrich.
Next, we explore the dungeon until the Profaned Capital, a place forgotten by time yet filled with riches scattered on the ground. Returning to Lothric, we venture into a beautiful castle under the red light of a bloody eclipse. There is also a secret, dark, and faded area of the starting zone that brings a strange, nostalgic sensation, before we finally arrive at the Furnace of the First Flame, buried in ashes and weapons under the eclipse's sun to finish the game.
The DLCs also bring remarkable locations: first, a frozen forest and a decaying village that strongly resembles Resident Evil, where we recognize Priscilla's tower from the Painted World of Ariamis. The second DLC starts in a completely chaotic jumble of kingdoms piled on top of each other, where we find the ruins of Earthen Peak and the first game's Firelink Shrine in the Demon Prince arena. Finally, we reach the Ringed City, a colossal city dedicated to the Pygmies with beautiful architecture, where the statue of Gwyn giving a crown to a pygmy king struck me the most. After Filianore, we are transported to the end of the world in a vast desert of ash, not to mention Midir's arena, which is the exact same place where the Furtive Pygmy finds the Dark Soul in the first game's cutscene.
• Soundtrack
 I am delighted to say that this game has the best OST of the entire Dark Souls trilogy. Upon starting the game, the very first screen greets us with one of the most beautiful pieces of music ever created for the saga, An epic piece of music with intense choruses that makes us feel like an era is ending, A truly fitting piece of music that evokes and does justice to the end times, perfectly matching the conclusion the franchise deserves.
 The tracks of the boss fights are truly incredible, so much so that I often hear them while working out at the gym haha. For me, the most striking song is Soul of Cinder; in it we hear intense choruses and Especially the second part of it, which is reminiscent of Gwyn's music from the first game; while this music plays, the boss makes the exact same movements as Gwyn, making it clear that Gwyn is still alive, inside of that legion of Lords of Cinder.
 Finally, the game's soundtrack shines, especially during boss fights; it perfectly matches the game's fast pace, encouraging us to face our challenges with fluidity and quick reflexes.
 The tracks I liked most were: Dark Souls III, Soul of Cinder, Iudex Gundyr, Vordt of the Boreal Valley, Pontiff Sulyvahn, Dancer of the Boreal Valley, Abyss Watchers, Yhorm the Giant and Sister Friede.
